targets.title: Largest subset of the 7^3 grid with no five points on a sphere or plane

best_known.source: AlphaEvolve repository of problems, problem 60 (arXiv:2511.02864, section 6.40)

targets.notes: Published construction reproduced by the verifier. Demonstrandum (June 2026) and Numaro (July 2026) reproduced the n = 7..12 values without improving them; Demonstrandum's symmetric search stalls one pair short at n = 11, 12 and its fitted law C(n) = floor((5n+7)/2) matches n = 7..14. The HuggingFace dataset dougdotcon/douvras-no-5-on-a-sphere-certificates only re-verifies these six sets. arXiv 2506.18113 settles only the asymptotics.

significance.evidence: Four public sources on 2026-09-24: AlphaEvolve set the value (arXiv:2511.02864, 2025); Demonstrandum (June 2026) and Numaro (July 2026) reproduced the n = 7..12 values without improving them; the HuggingFace dataset dougdotcon/douvras-no-5-on-a-sphere-certificates re-verifies the six AlphaEvolve sets.
significance.open_question: Demonstrandum's fitted law C(n) = floor((5n+7)/2), exact for the records at n = 7..14 and unproved beyond, and the gap to the trivial upper bound 4n.
